title: Panel simulator: interview catalog + day 1–60 skill map
content:
Purpose:
This working doc bundles two complementary artifacts we want people-ops + hiring managers to use: 1) a lightweight interview-panel simulator (catalog of short exercises + scoring rubric) to train interviewers and calibrate panels; 2) a pragmatic Day 1→Day 60 skills progression and check-in cadence to accelerate new hires in engineering and product roles. The intent: faster interviewer calibration, fewer bad signals in debriefs, and repeatable early success plans for hires.

How to use this doc (quick):
- People Ops runs a 60–90 minute panel-simulator session every quarter with at least one hiring manager and 3 interviewers from each hiring pool (SWE, ML infra, Product).
- Use the catalog below to pick 2 exercises per discipline (15–25 minutes each). Have one volunteer act as candidate; rest are panel. Score using the rubric. Debrief immediately.
- After hire, attach the Day1–60 skills map to the candidate's onboarding doc and schedule the check-ins listed in the calendar.

Part A — Panel simulator: catalog of exercises (pick 2)
Notes: exercises are designed to run in 18 minutes: 2 min setup, 12 min candidate response / pair-program or design sketch, 4 min focused clarifying questions and score.

Software Engineer (backend / infra focused)
- Exercise A1: "Cache Stampede Rescue" — Candidate is handed a small service design: read-heavy recommendation API behind a cache. Load spikes lead to cache stampedes and inconsistent responses. Prompt: identify root causes, propose two mitigation strategies (including tradeoffs), and sketch an experiment to validate the fix.
- Exercise A2: "Latency Regression Debugging" — Show traces (synthetic) with tail latency increase after a deploy. Candidate must interpret traces, list probable causes, suggest triage steps and a rollback vs mitigation decision.
- Small coding prompt (optional): microservice function to merge multiple sorted token streams with O(n) memory. Focus on clarity and edge cases.

ML / Inference Engineer (serving/runtime emphasis)
- Exercise B1: "KV Cache Reuse" — Given an autoregressive model serving flow, ask candidate to describe where KV cache can be safely reused across requests, pitfalls with multi-tenancy and privacy, and a fallback strategy when cache is invalidated.
- Exercise B2: "Quantization Tradeoffs" — Provide a short model profile (fp16 size, perf on T4/GPU), ask candidate to recommend a quantization path for latency vs quality tradeoffs and a lightweight A/B eval to detect regressions in hallucination rate.
- Hands-on: prompt-generation task for model: write a short prompt that enforces JSON output for structured metadata extraction; discuss failure modes.

Product / PM (inference product angle)
- Exercise C1: "Route policy for mixed tier" — Given a product that should route customers between cheaper quantized model and premium full-precision model, design a routing policy that balances SLA, cost, and quality degradation risk.
- Exercise C2: "Feature rollout + fallback" — Given a new streaming latency optimization, create an A/B rollout with error budget guardrails and rollback triggers.

Calibrated scoring rubric (panel use)
- Score each exercise on three axes: Problem Understanding (0–4), Solution Rigor (0–4), Communication & Tradeoffs (0–2). Total max = 10.
- Quick guidance: 0-3 = mismatch / unclear; 4-6 = acceptable / needs coaching; 7-8 = solid; 9-10 = exceptional.
- Red flags to record: makes unsafe assumptions about multi-tenancy / data privacy, dismisses observable telemetry, cannot prioritize tradeoffs.

Example debrief template (post-sim):
- What did the candidate do well? (1–3 bullets)
- Biggest gap or unknown?
- One suggested probing question to use in a real interview (text)
- Calibration rating by panel (average score)
- Action items for panelists (e.g., adjust question wording, clarify ideal answer range)

Part B — Day 1 → Day 60 skills progression (compact)
Notes: this is a lightweight skeleton you should paste into each hire's onboarding doc and adapt to role/level. The goal is measurable signals of success at 30d and 60d.

Day 0–7 (onboarding logistics + first week wins)
- Objectives: environment setup (repo access, dev machine, infra creds), meet buddy and manager, understand 1–2 high-level production flows.
- Deliverables: confirm access checklist, pair with buddy for a small bugfix PR and merge it to staging, 30-min stakeholder intro.
- Check-in: Manager 1:1 on Day 3; Buddy async notes on Day 5.

Day 8–30 (context + contribution)
- Objectives: own a small end-to-end change, understand perf and error dashboards for area, and ship a low-risk change.
- Deliverables: 1 merged feature or improvement with tests, public doc summarizing area architecture (500–800 words), join one oncall rotation shadow (if applicable).
- Signal of success at 30d: shipped change in mainline, demonstrates ability to explain tradeoffs for their code, consistently runs local integration tests.

Day 31–60 (ownership + impact)
- Objectives: deliver a measurable improvement (latency/cost/quality), lead a demo, identify a cross-team dependency and present mitigation plan.
- Deliverables: 1 impact PR (e.g., caching optimization, monitoring alert reduction), a readout doc for stakeholders, updated personal dev plan with goals for Q1.
- Signal of success at 60d: independent handling of code reviews, leads incident postmortem writeup if P0 occurred, measurable metric improvement or validated experiment plan.

Weekly check-in cadence (first 8 weeks)
- Manager 1:1: weekly (30–45 min) — focus on blockers, 30/60-day goals, feedback.
- Buddy sync: twice weekly (15 min) first 2 weeks, then weekly through week 8.
- Hiring manager health check (people ops): automated note at 30d and 60d to confirm signals and escalate coaching needs.

Buddy responsibilities (practical list)
- Day 0 checklist walkthrough and repo pointers, pair on first PR, introduce to three cross-team partners, triage one small bug together, summarize signals for manager at 30d.

Triage table for common onboarding blockers (use as checklist)
- No repo access: escalate to infra with ticket template (include IAM id, team, repos).
- Failing tests locally: ask for exact command and error logs, schedule paired debugging session.
- Can't reproduce prod bug: capture replay steps, request perf traces, loop in SRE.

Sample hiring plan snippet (for role-level alignment)
- Req: Senior ML Engineer (serving/runtime) — target funnel: 20 screened -> 6 onsites -> 1 hire in 8 weeks. Milestones: panel calibration session (wk 0), 6-panel interviews scheduled (wk 1–4), offer extension (wk 6).
- Interview slate: 1 coding (SWE), 1 infra/serving design (ML), 1 product or cross-functional, 1 behavioral loop with manager.

Open questions / TODOs (people-ops owners)
- Should we standardize the exercise bank per level (L3/L4/L5) with explicit expectations per score? (Priya owns draft)
- Build small repo with automated traces and sample inputs for latency regression exercises (Diego owns POC)
- Add a trimmed version of the rubric to the hiring packet for candidates (Rachel to coordinate with comms)

Appendix: quick templates
- Debrief micro-form (copy into Interview folder): candidate name, exercise, panel avg score, 3 bullets strengths, 3 bullets concerns, hire/no-hire vote.
- Manager 30/60 note template: 30d: "Has completed X, demonstrated Y, needs support Z"; 60d: "Independent on A, improved metric B by C% (or validated plan)".

This doc is intentionally compact. Use it as a living draft — update exercises and rubric after each quarterly panel-sim session.
